worldcombat.skill.stringshot.summary: Shoot a flying strand of silk in any direction to bind the first foe it touches, harshly lowering its Speed and briefly pinning its feet; a strand that misses sticks to the surface it actually strikes, leaving a small web. The Net posture spins the same strand into a slightly larger patch.
worldcombat.skill.stringshot.use.0: Stop a charging or fleeing enemy
worldcombat.skill.stringshot.description: A truly bound target loses %1$s Speed stage(s) and carries the Silked mark for %2$s; no symbol appears when Speed is already at its floor or an ability blocks it. While silked a companion will not re-strand it. The Speed drop is a stat stage that lasts until the target leaves combat or its stat stages are reset. A Bind hit also pins it in place for %3$s, unable to move.

The Net posture spins the same strand into a slightly larger web: it sticks on the outside of the first block struck, spreading at most %1$s blocks of radius for %2$s; when it cannot be placed only decorative silk remains, and no web appears at a far target point out of thin air.

The strand is a flying projectile: speed %1$s with a %2$s hit radius, blocked by cover and dodgeable by movement; it reaches %3$s blocks over a %4$s range and winds up for %5$s. Hitting a block leaves a small web taut on that surface; spending itself in open air leaves nothing.
worldcombat.skill.stringshot.timing: Range %1$s blocks, windup %2$s, recovery %3$s, costs %4$s PP, cooldown %5$s.
On: the strand spreads a slightly larger sticky web on the surface it first strikes, with longer reach, but no pin and a slower windup and longer cooldown. Off: bind one target with a fast shot that also pins it briefly. Both postures only leave a web when the strand actually strikes a surface.
The companion only considers a strand while a threat is within this many blocks; smaller keeps it at point-blank, larger starts earlier.
In Net posture the companion only spins the larger patch with at least this many enemies around the target; 1 means lay it on sight.
In Bind posture, when on, the companion only strands fleeing threats to hold them; off, it will strand any threat in range.
When on, the companion may leave its post to strand under a Hold order.
